title: US Data Center Construction Hits Record 211% Growth Pace
summary:
The surge in spending on the physical facilities needed for generative AI has propelled the expansion of the US data hub market to a historic high. The sector's quarterly annualized growth rate reached 211%, increasing its share of the nation's total construction spending to 4.3% from 2% at the start of 2025.

This growth follows a general decline in the building sector, with total US construction spending falling 1.9% in September to an annualized $2.186 trillion, the largest monthly contraction since April 2020. While private nonresidential construction rose 1.1% for the fourth consecutive month, spending on private residential projects dropped 5.5%.

US DATA CENTER CONSTRUCTION SURGES AT RECORD PACE DESPITE SPENDING SLUMP

US construction spending fell 1.9% in September, but underlying momentum remains strong, supported by AI infrastructure investment.

Data center construction surged at a record 211% quarterly annualized pace, with monthly growth of 8–10% over the past four months.

Private nonresidential construction rose 1.1%, its fourth consecutive monthly gain, while residential spending dropped 5.5%.

Data centers now account for 4.3% of total construction spending, up from 2% in early 2025.
